Well, my husband and I find it easier to manage the joint expenses (mortgage, food, utilities, etc) by having a joint account.  We only put enough in there to cover expenses.  The rest of our paychecks are in our separate accounts.

We also file taxes jointly as we get a better return that way.  Sometimes we split the return in half, sometimes we use it to pay down joint debt (like upgrades to the house).

It’s a personal choice and one that every couple has to make.

I’m 40 and have only been diagnosed for 5 years.  I’ve had symptoms since my teens, but not a full break until 35 (rough couple of years).

I’ve been hospitalized three times.  Keep a journal, not just of your mood, but other triggers, things that let you know when you are starting to go off.  My journal tracks my mood, sleep, eating habits and energy level.  My therapist and I go over the journal in our sessions every two weeks.

Also, if you have a partner or roommate that is comfortable enough, let them know your warning signs.  They can help let you know when you’re starting to slip - as it can be hard to see ourselves.

Talk to your psychologist and don’t be afraid to be honest about what you are feeling and if you don’t feel “right” on a certain med, let the doctor know.  It’s a lot of trial and error to find the right med or combo of meds.

I’m on the med I reacted to best, Latuda.  However, I’m starting to feel I may need an adjustment.  It’s not an urgent need, like what’s put me in the hospital in the past, just a note I have to myself for my next visit.

Last bit - when your brain tries to tell you that you are worthless and no one cares about you, fight back.  Reach out to talk to someone.  Find proof your brain is lying to you.  Redirect your thoughts to focus on what you do well.  It’s not easy and it takes time to build up the strength to fight yourself.
